events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.50 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The trip ran 11.6 km against an 8.4 km optimal route, +3.2 km, and the fare record bills 3.19 km of deviation from the billed distance against the optimal route, above the 1 km tolerance, so a refund is triggered [F1][F4][RD-1]. The whole deviation sits in one off-route segment, 12:11–12:17, which drove 4.45 km where the optimal route covers 1.58 km, adding 2.88 km and driving CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 among its roads [F3][RD-1].

The rider's consent has to be read from its words: the driver asked at 12:07 "shall I take another way?" and the rider answered at 12:08 "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4." [F7][F8]. That is a yes to a route choice made by the driver, but it is bounded: the rider expressly ruled out one road, and the consent is then a general route choice with that road excluded. The code checks the named road against the roads the segment drove; the excluded road, CLEMENTI AVENUE 4, was in fact driven, so the agreement does not reach the segment [F3][F8][RD-5]. A general yes with a road ruled out leaves that road outside the consent; the segment therefore counts under RD-2, and there is no exempt km [F8][F3][RD-5][RD-2].

The driver's assertion in his written statement that "the rider said can, so I went round" is a post-trip claim, not consent, and adds nothing beyond the chat [F10][RD-5]. RD-3 is not engaged: the rider never named a place or route the car was to go to; she named only a road to be avoided [F8][RD-3]. The traffic record is not decisive for the amount: the congestion on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (band 2, active 11:58–12:17) gives the segment a traffic reason, so no driver violation is recorded on that ground, but under RD-2 the amount still turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for this route, and she did not [F11][F3][RD-4][RD-2][RD-5].

Amount, from the trace's arithmetic and the numbers on record: (3.19 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4096/km = $4.50, which matches the excess distance item billed for 3.19 km at this trip's distance fare [$F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; there is no surge on this trip [F4][F5][F6][FARE-0][RD-2]. The outcome is refund_partial $4.50, consistent as well with the fare-dispute and route-deviation precedents of the same shape (DISP-2026-0089, DISP-2026-0142) [PREC-1]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver's one upheld dispute in 90 days is not a route deviation (route: 0), so no account flag [F17][RD-6].
